findings.title: Multiple date-override ranges on the same day make most slots unavailable
findings.body: `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns true (slot rejected) as soon as ANY override range on that day does not contain the slot. A host with two override intervals on one date (e.g. 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00) is a supported setup. A slot at 14:30 is outside the first interval, so `find` returns true on it and the slot is rejected even though it is inside the second. The check needs to pass when the slot fits in at least one same-day override, and fail only when it fits in none. As written, the new logic wrongly drops valid slots for fixed hosts, and for collective and loose hosts too, since all of them now go through this check.

findings.title: Slots that only partially overlap a date override are treated as available
findings.body: The override test only rejects a slot if `slotEnd <= override.start` or `slotStart > override.end`. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it is accepted. A slot that starts inside the override and ends after `override.end` is accepted. A slot starting exactly at `override.end` is accepted, because `isAfter` is strict. Example: with a fixed-host override of 10:00-11:00, a 10:30-11:30 or 11:00-12:00 slot generated from another host's availability passes. This is the situation the PR is meant to prevent (RR events booked when the fixed host is unavailable). The condition should be that the whole slot lies in `[override.start, override.end]`, i.e. reject when `slotStart < start` or `slotEnd > end`.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === (always false)
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct object references, so it is never true. The intended "zero-length override means unavailable" branch is dead code. Use `.isSame()` or compare the underlying values.

findings.title: Working-hours check is wrong: `end` equals `start`, and multiple ranges per day reject everything
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()` is identical to `start`. It should be based on the slot end time, so a slot that runs past the end of working hours is never caught. The `find` also returns true (slot unavailable) whenever any working-hours entry for that weekday does not contain the slot. Users with split schedules (e.g. 09-12 and 13-17) produce two entries for the same day, and any slot is outside at least one of them, so nearly all slots are rejected. Because this check is now applied to every fixed and loose host, it is a regression for those schedules. It should reject only when no entry contains the slot. Working hours are also compared against the UTC weekday and minutes of the slot, which needs care for schedules that cross UTC midnight.

findings.title: Override-to-slot matching uses the UTC calendar day and breaks for overrides crossing UTC midnight
findings.body: An override is matched to a slot only when the UTC date of the shifted `override.start` equals the UTC date of `slotStartTime`. For organizers far from UTC, an override that begins on one UTC day and ends on the next (e.g. 10:00-18:00 PST is 18:00-02:00 UTC) will not match slots falling on the second UTC day. Those slots are then treated as having no override and fall through to the normal working-hours/busy logic. This can wrongly allow or deny them, which defeats the override.

findings.title: Timezone-shifted overrides can wrap past midnight and land on the wrong invitee day
findings.body: The override is selected for an invitee day by `activeOverrides` using the unshifted (organizer-wall-clock-as-UTC) `override.start`. Only afterwards is the invitee-organizer offset added and reduced to `hour()*60+minute()`. Two problems follow. (1) If the shift pushes the start/end past midnight, the minutes wrap modulo 24h, so start or end becomes a small number and the range is either dropped (`start >= end` is skipped in `buildSlots`) or shown on the wrong day. (2) The day the override is attached to is computed before the shift. With a large timezone gap (e.g. organizer in Kolkata with a 20:00-23:00 override, invitee in Tokyo) the override can be attached to the day after the one it really falls on. The shifted instant, not the raw one, should be used for both the day filter and the minute-of-day computation.

findings.title: Parsing `override.start.toString()` is lossy and environment-dependent
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` goes through `Date.prototype.toString()`, which yields a locale/host-timezone formatted string without milliseconds that is re-parsed by the engine. Pass `override.start` directly. Also `override.timeZone` is optional in `TimeRange`, and `.tz(undefined)` silently falls back to the default zone instead of failing visibly.

findings.title: Fixed-host round-robin date-override fix has no test; new timezone test is weak
findings.body: The headline fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides must be respected in round-robin events, but no test covers it: no scenario with a fixed host that has an override and a round-robin host that does not. None covers multiple override ranges on one day, slots overlapping an override boundary, or overrides crossing midnight or UTC midnight, which are exactly where the new logic is fragile. The added timezone test (Dhaka) only shifts by 30 minutes and expects identical UTC slots. The `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher also passes when the actual list is shorter than the expected list, so missing slots would go unnoticed.
